checks.invariant: Model output can supply only a bounded patch against the selected source; it cannot supply shell syntax, Git metadata, a repository URL, or publication credentials.
checks.result: generatePatch reparses strict output and reruns guardPatch. verifyPatch clones the source, reparses the patch, binds commit and blob identities, rejects unsafe targets, and recalculates actual changes. Git path arguments follow --, Git hooks/fsmonitor/protocols are disabled by the sandbox environment, and configured commands are argv supplied by operator configuration. Repository names are encoded into a fixed HTTPS GitHub API origin with redirects rejected. Branch and outbound text normalization prevent control-character/ref injection. No direct model-to-shell or model-selected external URL bypass was established.

checks.invariant: The Project that owns the Work item must also be authorized for the repository whose source reaches the model and whose GitHub installation publishes its patch.
checks.result: The daemon and durable reads bind caller.projectId, but contextClient selects from one boot-wide policy.github.repos using only snapshot.item.service. RepoPolicy and the policy context have no Project binding. A Project-scoped plugin service is caller-selected, and an own-Project Deployment accepts a syntactically valid SHA without a repository association. The final publication check repeats only the service-to-repo relationship. This leaves a source-grounded Project-to-repository authorization candidate; it does not require bypassing the existing Project guards or assuming prompt injection succeeds.

unresolved: No bounded two-Project fixture was executed because the assignment prohibits target execution and complete OS-enforced memory and cumulative-disk sandbox controls are unavailable.

The owner must establish whether the shared deployment grants otherwise unrelated Projects and whether the repository policy intentionally grants every such Project access to the same service-named repository.

checks.invariant: Publication requires durable admission and an owned attempt; uncertain effects block replacement publication, while known references survive transport and optional-label failures.
checks.result: The daemon audits before publication, saves a fenced intent before publish, records a known PR before completion, and preserves uncertain admission after branch/draft failures. API transitions bind Project, command, versions, lease/worker, repository, branch and base; a recorded PrRef cannot be replaced. Replays and answers share replayWork; recovery is read-only against GitHub. The production executor supplies no test runner override; gitChecks is reached from test fixtures only. The production package exports the verified publication path and no merge operation. No duplicate-write or transition bypass was established apart from recovery's weaker object binding.

checks.invariant: Retry and reconciliation must accept only the same verified publication object admitted by the original attempt.
checks.result: PublicationIntent stores only repo, branch and baseSha. getExistingDraft requires a unique open draft in the same repository, matching ref/head, and one parent equal to the base. It does not check the head tree against the verified patch or an expected head digest. reconcile then records that reference and finishes completed without source verification. Normal publishVerified also returns an existing matching draft before writing the verified patch. A same-parent replacement tree therefore survives all source-visible recovery checks if a lower-trust repository writer can mutate that branch.

unresolved: A harmless same-parent/different-tree transport fixture and recovery replay were not executed because target execution is prohibited and the complete audit sandbox is unavailable.
Repository rulesets and who can rewrite the bot branch are external facts; no live repository was inspected.

checks.invariant: Patch and source paths cannot escape the workspace, alias Git metadata, overlap repository files/directories, or introduce ambiguous casing or source modes.
checks.result: The guards reject absolute, backslash, NUL, empty, dot and parent components, enforce allowed/forbidden globs, reject case-folded duplicates, and additionally reject control characters and every .git component. Selected source entries permit only regular/executable blob modes, reject case collisions and file/directory collisions, and validate content hashes. validatePatchTargets compares against the full repository metadata, including excluded symlinks, before writes. Workspace construction uses a fresh private directory, exclusive initial writes and per-component symlink checks. Ordinary traversal and static alias paths stop at these checks; concurrent post-command ownership is assessed in its separate assigned unit.

checks.invariant: File counts, source bytes, binary source and actual additions/deletions must be bounded before publication, independent of the model's reported metadata.
checks.result: REST limits a tree to 20,000 entries and rejects truncation, limits decoded blobs to 1 MiB and responses to 8 MiB, checks base64 identity/size, decodes UTF-8 fatally and rejects NULs. prepareSource limits selected files to 200 and total selected content to 1 MiB, verifies blob hashes, and checks declared and actual bytes. guardPatch bounds files and complete content line counts. verifyPatch computes actual numstat with external diff/textconv/renames disabled, requires exactly the proposed changed paths, and reruns the line guard using actual additions plus deletions, including deletions reported as zero by the model. Tests were inspected as source only. No surviving static path/file-count or underreported-deletion bypass was found.

checks.invariant: After each check, the parent accepts only the proposed regular files and preserved modes, and publishes from immutable verified memory rather than reopening workspace files.
checks.result: assertWorkspace checks root identity, symlinks, expected directory prefixes, regular-file entries, exact byte size, executable status, content and missing files after every configured check. The verifier holds a parsed in-memory patch and hashes the complete receipt; publication does not consume later workspace bytes. Existing root-symlink, content-mutation and mode-mutation tests were read only. No static replacement-to-publication substitution was established. The walk uses separate readdir/lstat/readFile operations, so the assumption that sandbox writers have terminated remains important.

checks.invariant: Every untrusted descendant must terminate before host-side workspace inspection and cleanup begin.
checks.result: execute kills only the initial detached process group. The macOS policy permits fork and same-sandbox child groups and has no process namespace or descendant supervisor. A child that starts another session with ignored stdio can therefore remain a potential workspace writer after the foreground command closes; a child retaining stdout can instead keep close pending beyond the timer. The existing process test explicitly exercises a detached child group but kills it itself. This unit links the process-lifetime root cause; it does not claim a demonstrated host-file disclosure or publication of workspace bytes.

unresolved: The macOS descendant/session behavior and continued writer lifetime require a bounded dummy-process check. No target-controlled process can be run under the present execution prohibition and incomplete memory/cumulative-disk sandbox.

checks.invariant: Accepted source/model work must have command cardinality, elapsed-time, output and policy-admission bounds before consuming shared verifier resources.
checks.result: verifyPatch requires 1-20 argv commands with at most 100 arguments each and a 1-120,000 ms total command deadline; every sandbox call receives the remaining budget. Source and patch guards constrain intake, stdout is capped at 2 MiB, and policy checks confidence, diagnosis, publication and spend counters. The HTTP handler also bounds request bytes and response wait time. These bounds do not settle descendant lifetime because timeout enforcement relies on one process group and on receiving close; the inspected timeout test covers only a directly sleeping command.

checks.invariant: A repository-controlled check cannot retain a daemon operation or child process after its deadline by changing its process group or keeping inherited output open.
checks.result: On macOS the sandbox permits child groups, while stop sends SIGKILL only to -child.pid. The timer neither rejects the promise independently nor waits for every descendant. A detached descendant holding stdout can delay the sole close handler after the timeout; an ignored-stdio descendant can survive successful return. The former retains the Work promise and can continue lease heartbeats, while drainCommands awaits all pending operations. The Linux bubblewrap path has a separate PID-namespace control, so this candidate is limited to the macOS adapter. No saturation, OOM or disk-exhaustion result is claimed.

unresolved: A strictly bounded macOS fixture must observe one detached descendant and elapsed completion time past a short verifier deadline; no such execution was authorized or performed.
Actual verification commands and outer process supervision are operator-owned deployment facts. The path requires a configured command that executes repository-controlled code.

checks.invariant: Fresh publication must use the same Deployment commit, source tree, blob identities, patch contents and file modes that verification accepted.
checks.result: Source is read at the Deployment SHA rather than mutable branch HEAD. Blob hashes and base identities are checked before verification. The in-process WeakMap receipt covers the full verified result and snapshot hash, and publication checks it before cloning the source, policy and patch. A fresh draft uses the recorded base tree and commit parent, creates blobs from the verified in-memory patch, and preserves original executable modes. The deterministic branch identity incorporates incident, snapshot and patch hashes. No fresh-publication object substitution through workspace mutation or branch HEAD movement was found.

checks.invariant: An already-existing or recovered draft must be bound to the same immutable verified content as a newly created draft.
checks.result: The expected patch/snapshot hashes influence the branch name but are not verified against the remote head tree. PublicationPlan and persisted PublicationIntent omit expected head/tree identity. REST recovery validates the current PR head against the current ref and original parent, so a different current tree with that same parent passes. Both publishVerified's existing-draft shortcut and replay reconciliation consume the weaker result. Existing source tests reject moved refs, wrong parents, merge commits and repository mismatches, but contain no different-tree/same-parent rejection. This is the same root cause as the business-logic candidate.

unresolved: No transport fixture was executed to demonstrate acceptance of a different tree with the same parent; target execution is prohibited and complete memory/cumulative-disk sandbox controls are absent.
The owner must confirm that an actor below Graveshift's verification authority can update the generated branch under the actual GitHub rulesets.

checks.invariant: The verifier's untrusted child does not receive daemon/provider/GitHub credentials, arbitrary host filesystem access or network authority through the source-visible launch path.
checks.result: sandboxEnv builds an explicit environment with scratch HOME/TMPDIR and safe Git configuration instead of spreading process.env. The macOS profile denies network, host writes, general reads outside enumerated tool/system paths, host signaling, process inspection, mach lookup and Apple events. Linux requires bubblewrap with --unshare-all, no capabilities, read-only tool binds and only the workspace writable; a network namespace alone is rejected. A failed isolation probe or absent sandbox fails closed. All command invocations use the adapter, including initial Git operations. Tests were read only, so this is source control coverage, not a claim of exercised OS enforcement. The separately linked descendant-lifetime issue does not establish a host credential escape.

checks.invariant: Credential-bearing GitHub calls remain in the trusted daemon and occur only through the verified publication path; test adapters must not become a production sandbox bypass.
checks.result: main constructs executorFromEnv without a runner override. GitHub App signing, installation-token acquisition/cache and authenticated fixed-origin REST calls stay in the parent process. createFixExecutor's injectable runner is used by test fixtures; fix-recording is not imported by production main. The package exports verifyPatch and verified publication, and the GitHub interface exposes draft publication with no merge operation. Cancellation is checked before each GitHub method and audit/admission gates precede writes. No additional credential-bearing execution path or production use of the unisolated recording runner was found.

candidates.title: Service-only repository selection lacks a Project authorization binding
candidates.description: A principal authorized only for its own Project can supply that Project's service name and register a known Deployment SHA. When the daemon serves that Project alongside another Project, contextClient chooses a GitHub repository from the shared policy solely by service name. For an otherwise eligible Fix with a valid generated patch, the daemon then reads source and can publish a draft in that repository using its GitHub App installation, even though the caller has no repository authority. The source-visible Project and Organization checks remain intact; the missing control is the relationship between that authenticated Project and the selected repository. The intended repository ownership/grant policy and a bounded observed wrong-target result still require validation.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: apps/daemon/src/fix-context.ts filters policy.github.repos only by snapshot.item.service. Neither RepoPolicy nor the boot policy repository schema records an allowed Project, and the final publication check only repeats service membership. Thus the Project identity used to protect durable state is dropped before selecting GitHub source and publication authority.

trace.description: An authenticated own-Project Fix request passes the granted-Project check, reads that Project's Work item and claims its attempt; no repository authority is attached to the caller.
The claimed attempt resolves context with the authenticated caller and its Project-scoped Work snapshot.

The repository is selected from the instance policy using only service membership. Subsequent context consistency checks bind Project-owned incident/diagnosis/deployment facts but never bind that Project to the chosen repository.
open_pr admission uses the shared service/category/signals/confidence/counter context, which has no Project-to-repository authorization fact. Audit success and policy allowance are still required.

The trusted GitHub client reads the selected repository at the supplied Project's bound Deployment SHA. Repository source enters the model call at line 131, and any valid generated patch proceeds through verifyPatch at line 146.
Publication admission persists the chosen repo/branch/base under the caller's Project before invoking the prepared publication; it does not add a repository ownership check.
The last repository allowlist gate checks incident.service against repo.services and the patch path rules, with no Project selector.

The daemon uses its installation-backed GitHub client to create a draft in the selected repository. The unauthorized effect to validate is the cross-Project repository read or draft write, not a merge or guaranteed malicious model output.

evidence.description: One command runtime receives all boot.projectIds and one shared boot.policy/contextClient.
Internal boot returns the daemon's full Project grant alongside the one global policy.
Repository selection requires exactly one matching service mapping but never includes caller.projectId.
Repository policy contains repo/services/baseBranch/branchPrefix/path rules but no allowed Project or Organization.
A delegated Credential binds the caller's Project and stores the requested service value; it does not reserve that service name across Projects.
Event guards enforce the credential's own Project/service and an own-Project Deployment lookup. They do not establish ownership of a GitHub repository named by a matching global service policy.
Deployment creation correctly checks own-Organization/Project authority, then stores the caller-supplied SHA without associating it with a repository. The DTO checks a 40-hex form.
The final publication target check is service membership only; the GitHub installation is selected later from the resulting repository string.

blockers: No target-controlled function harness or test was executed: source-only execution is required, and complete OS-enforced memory and cumulative-disk limits for audit execution are unavailable.

The owner must confirm that the actual shared daemon can serve an attacker-controlled Project and a repository intended for another Project, and that the operator did not intentionally grant that repository to every granted Project with the same service name.

An end-to-end draft-write demonstration requires an otherwise eligible own-Project diagnosis/Work item, a known commit in the selected repository, configured verification, and a valid model patch. These conditions must be supplied by dummy fixtures rather than assumed from prompt injection.

validation_plan.local: After a complete OS sandbox is approved, use two dummy Projects and one fake GitHub repository intended for only the first. Return valid own-Project context for the second Project with the same service name and a harmless known base SHA. Invoke contextClient and record whether it selects the first Project's repository. If needed, use a fake gateway, sandbox runner and recording GitHub client to show a valid one-line patch reaches createPullRequest for that repository without network or real credentials. The regression must reject repository selection before the first source read unless the authenticated Project is explicitly granted that repository.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner should inspect the configured daemon Project grant, intended repository ownership, and whether service names are expected to be reusable across Organizations. This is a configuration review only; do not send events or Fix requests to a deployed service.

candidates.title: Publication recovery can accept a same-parent head with unverified content
candidates.description: A repository actor able to rewrite a generated bot branch can replace its head with a different tree whose sole parent is the admitted Deployment SHA. If the draft is still open and the attempt needs reconciliation, recovery checks the current PR head against the current ref and original parent, then records that draft as the completed Fix. It never compares the remote tree to the verified patch. The branch name includes verified hashes, but a writer can retain that name while changing its content. The affected boundary is Graveshift's verification/result authority: the candidate claims acceptance of an unverified draft head, not GitHub write privilege gain for a writer, automatic merge, or release execution. Branch permissions and a bounded acceptance result remain unvalidated.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The immutable object identity is lost when planPublication reduces the receipt to repo/branch/baseSha and PublicationIntent persists only those fields. getExistingDraft binds the current head/ref to the base parent but does not bind its tree or head digest to the original verified result. Both existing-draft reuse and uncertain-effect reconciliation trust this weaker identity.

trace.description: An authenticated replay of an uncertain publication parses the persisted intent containing repo, branch and baseSha, with no expected result tree or head. The lower-trust input is the current remote branch/PR state a repository writer can have replaced.
Recovery forwards only the recorded repository, mutable branch name and base SHA to the GitHub client and checks the returned repository/branch.
The client requires a unique open draft with the exact head ref in the same repository, preventing fork/ref confusion but not modification of the named branch.

It reads the remote commit's SHA and parents plus the current ref. The schema omits tree identity; acceptance requires only matching current head/ref and one parent equal to the recorded base. A different tree with that parent satisfies these checks.
The returned head reference is recorded under the original attempt and base. API recordPublication checks intent repository/branch/base and known-reference equality, not the verified tree.

The Work attempt is finished as completed with ok:true and the recovered head, without rerunning source verification. The minimal result to validate is recording a harmless substituted tree as the verified Fix.

evidence.description: planPublication validates the local receipt but returns only repository, deterministic branch and original base SHA.
Snapshot and patch hashes influence the branch name; they are not independently recovered from remote content.
The durable PublicationIntent schema has no expected head, expected tree or verified content digest.
The strongest remote check verifies PR head/ref consistency and a single parent equal to baseSha, with no content-identity comparison.
The normal publication path also returns a recovered existing draft immediately, without creating the verified content again or checking its remote tree.
The durable consumer checks repository/branch/base equality and fences state, but accepts the first recovered head because the intent has no expected content identity.
Source tests exercise wrong base, merge/root commits, moved refs and mismatched heads; no same-parent/different-tree binding is represented. These tests were not executed.

blockers: The assignment prohibits project execution, and the audit environment has no approved complete memory/cumulative-disk sandbox, so the same-parent/different-tree acceptance path has not been observed locally.

Actual GitHub rulesets, branch protections and the ability of a lower-trust repository actor to rewrite the bot branch are not visible in the reviewed source. A deployment that forbids such writes may prevent this attack condition.

A fixture must distinguish ordinary collaborator editing from a verification-authority failure by observing the exact substituted head being recorded as the original completed Fix; no broader release or merge consequence is established.

validation_plan.local: In an approved offline sandbox, use a recording REST transport and two harmless Git trees with the same base parent. Persist a real-shaped uncertain intent for the originally verified tree, then return an open draft whose named branch and current head both point to the second tree. Exercise getExistingDraft and daemon replay reconciliation with fake durable state. Observe whether the second head becomes the completed result, and also check publishVerified's existing-draft shortcut. A regression must require a persisted expected tree/head identity and reject the second object before recording completion. Use dummy hashes, no live GitHub, and no retained artifacts until parent promotion is available.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner should review which actors can create or force-update the generated branch namespace and whether rulesets prevent all lower-trust rewrites. No branch should be modified to check this fact.

candidates.title: macOS verifier cleanup targets one process group instead of all descendants
candidates.description: When a configured verification command executes repository-controlled code on macOS, that code can attempt to start a detached child in another process group. The source sandbox permits child creation, but the supervisor kills only the original command group. A descendant retaining inherited stdout can keep the close event and verification promise pending beyond the deadline; one using ignored stdio can instead remain alive after a successful return and during parent workspace inspection. This crosses the untrusted-check lifetime boundary into shared daemon work/process resources. The candidate is limited to retained work and potential concurrent writers; no host-file disclosure, actual service exhaustion or sandbox credential escape has been demonstrated.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: sandbox.execute treats process.kill(-child.pid) as complete teardown and resolves only from child.close. The macOS sandbox profile allows fork and same-sandbox child groups but supplies no descendant supervisor or process namespace. Changing session/group therefore falls outside the only kill target, while neither the timer nor verification independently terminates the pending operation or proves all writers are gone.

trace.description: A policy-accepted patch or repository file is executed by an operator-configured verification command. This condition requires a command that actually executes repository-controlled code; Git diff-only checks do not provide it.
The platform chooses sandbox-exec with macProfile. The policy permits process-fork and same-sandbox child operations, without Linux's PID namespace.
The trusted supervisor starts a detached command group with piped stdout. Repository-controlled code can attempt to create another detached group and retain the pipe or ignore stdio.
Cleanup and the timeout signal only -child.pid. They do not enumerate or own the detached descendant group, and the timer does not independently reject the promise.
Completion waits for close, which can remain pending while a separate descendant holds stdout. Conversely, ignored-stdio descendants need not prevent close and are not proven dead before returning.

While the verification promise remains pending, the attempt scope can continue its lease heartbeat; its finally block has not run. A closed-stdio survivor instead overlaps verifyPatch's post-command workspace inspection.

The daemon retains and drains pending Work promises, so a verification operation that outlives its deadline can also retain graceful drain. The minimal bounded observation is one dummy descendant or operation surviving a short deadline, not a stress test.

evidence.description: The sole termination target is the original negative child PID/process group.
The timer sets timedOut and calls stop but does not reject or resolve a still-open child result independently.
Only close resolves a running command; waiting on inherited stdout is therefore outside the timer's direct control.
The macOS policy permits process-fork. Unlike the Linux branch's --unshare-all path, it does not create a process namespace or bind all descendants to a supervisor-owned lifetime.

An existing source test intentionally spawns a detached child group from a sandboxed process and explicitly signals that group itself. It does not test supervisor cleanup after the parent exits or times out; the test was not run.
Host-side assertWorkspace follows a returned command, and finally removes the root at line 229 without a proof that every descendant has exited.
The HTTP handler bounds waiting with within(result), but the underlying command promise remains owned by drainCommands; this does not supply descendant cleanup.

blockers: The supported macOS sandbox-exec and runtime process/pipe lifecycle must be observed with a harmless detached-child fixture. Source declarations and unexecuted tests are insufficient to confirm OS behavior.

Target-controlled execution is prohibited for this assignment, and complete OS-enforced memory, process, CPU, per-file, cumulative-disk, filesystem and wall-clock controls for an audit fixture have not been established.

The deployed verifier must run on macOS with a command that executes repository-controlled code; actual configured commands and any outer descendant supervisor are operator-owned facts. The Linux PID-namespace path is not claimed vulnerable to this exact lifetime escape.

validation_plan.local: After the parent supplies a complete OS sandbox on a disposable macOS host, run one harmless fixture through runSandboxed with a short deadline. Have it spawn at most one detached child that self-terminates within a small fixed outer limit. In one case the child keeps stdout open; record whether the operation settles by its deadline. In a second case it ignores stdio and writes one dummy marker inside the fixture workspace after foreground completion; record whether it survived supervisor cleanup. Capture elapsed time and at most one PID/marker, then terminate and reap every fixture process. Do not fork repeatedly, allocate large memory, fill disk, inspect host processes, or access credentials. The regression must prove all descendants are gone before success, failure, timeout, post-command inspection and workspace removal.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner should inspect the daemon OS, the verification argv for the affected repository, and whether an outer job/process supervisor tears down every descendant. This is a read-only configuration review and does not require running a check on the deployed daemon.

hardening: The verifier installs time, input and stdout bounds but no explicit per-job CPU, memory, process-count or total-disk quotas. Add such controls to contain arbitrary verification code. This source-only review makes no separate OOM, fork-exhaustion or disk-exhaustion finding without a bounded shared-resource observation and review of outer deployment quotas.
